digest.component_or_area: tickets-branch CAS delivery and workflow orchestration
propositions: Duplicate CAS push and retry loops scattered across workflow definitions must be consolidated into a single Python core module to eliminate code duplication and establish a canonical delivery contract.

The strict push entrypoint must support both deterministic failure classification (policy decline vs transport failure) and exhaustion of a fixed retry budget, raising PushDeliveryError with stable reasons and unpushed-commit counts for automated callers.
Python core entrypoints must remain reusable and never call sys.exit; workflow failures must surface through a private adapter that translates typed core failures into process exit codes and stderr.
Existing best-effort callers (library, CLI, MCP, importer, ticket-store) must preserve their current behavior and return contracts when strict delivery is not explicitly requested.
Both reconciliation workflows (bridge and canary) must delegate outbound delivery exactly once to the strict Python adapter, eliminating their local fetch/merge/retry loops.
The locked commit-and-push transaction must handle dirty-tree preservation, stash restoration, author/subject contracts, and store-epoch guards without introducing new schema or event vocabulary.
